papers.title: Origin of homochirality in peptides: The first milestone at the origin of life
papers.authors: Søren Toxvaerd
papers.abstract: Living organisms have some common structures, chemical reactions, and molecular structures. The organisms consist of cells with cell division; they have homochirality of protein and carbohydrate units, metabolism, and genetics, and they are mortal. The molecular structures and chemical reactions underlying these features are common to all, from the simplest bacteria to human beings. The origin of life is evolutionary, with the emergence of a network of spontaneous biochemical reactions, and evolution has taken place over a very long time. The evolution contains, however, some ``landmarks'' and bottlenecks, which in a revolutionary manner directed the evolution, and the article establishes an order of some of these events. Recent articles show that peptides in living organisms are long-time unstable, with loss of their secondary homochiral conformations and with D-amino acids. Based on these observations and an extensive scientific literature on Abiogenesis, we argue that the first milestone in the prebiotic evolution is at the emergence of homochiral peptides in an aqueous solution with a high concentration of amino acids and a lower water activity than in the cytosol in living organisms. The homochiral peptides in cytosol are unstable, and the long-time aging of peptides in the cytosol causes mortality of living organisms. The metabolism and genetics are established in an environment with homochiral peptides in the Earth's crust for $\approx$ 4 Gyr ago at a lower water activity than in the cytosol in living organisms. Finally, the cells with cell division are established in the Hot Springs environment at the interface between the crust and the Hadean Ocean.

papers.title: The Late-time Afterglow of GW170817 and Implications for Jet Dynamics
papers.authors: Aman Katira, Kunal P. Mooley, Kenta Hotokezaka
papers.abstract: GW170817 is the first binary neutron star merger detected with gravitational and electromagnetic waves, and its afterglow is still detectable 7 years post-merger. Some previous studies of the X-ray afterglow have claimed the onset of a new afterglow component or raised concerns about the data processing techniques. Motivated thus, we present here a reanalysis of X-ray afterglow data for GW170817 and find potential sources of discrepancies between the data reduction techniques employed by various research groups. We also analyze the updated panchromatic afterglow data to find that there is no significant evidence for any new afterglow component (e.g. due to the ejecta that gave rise to the kilonova) and that the jet must be still in a mildly relativistic phase. The decline in the afterglow light curve is significantly shallower compared to that expected from the standard synchrotron afterglow jet models with sideways spreading, indicating either an additional energy injection at late times or the velocity dependence on the microphysics parameters. In this context, we discuss the implications of the late time afterglow data on jet dynamics.

papers.title: Second-scale periodicity in FRB 20201124A: coincident with critical RM evolution epochs and its possible implications
papers.authors: Wen-Long Zhang, Chen-Ran Hu, Chen Du, Zhen-Yin Zhao, Wang-Chen Xue, Wen-Jun Tan, Shuang-Xi Yi, Shao-Lin Xiong, Fa-Yin Wang, Li-Ming Song, Cheng-Kui Li, Shuang-Nan Zhang, Chen-Wei Wang, Sheng-Lun Xie, Xiao-Fei Dong, Yong-Feng Huang
papers.abstract: Second-timescale periodicity ($\sim$1.7\,s) has been reported in the repeating fast radio burst FRB\,20201124A during two epochs, MJD\,59310 and MJD\,59347. We find that these two epochs coincide with the days on which the Faraday rotation measure (RM) of the source passes through the transition between the quasi-steady and the strongly varying phases that are predicted by the magnetar/Be-star binary model. To examine whether this coincidence could arise by chance, we re-fitted the secular RM evolution within the same binary framework and estimated the probability of chance coincidence, $P_{\rm CC}\approx2.5\%$. Independently, and in order to cross-validate the reported periodicity, we carried out a coherent joint period search on the bursts of the two epochs, assuming a simple linear evolution of the spin period; we obtain $P_0=1.70603$\,s and $\dot{P}=6.1\times10^{-10}$\,s\,s$^{-1}$ at the reference epoch, with a Gaussian significance of $\sim3.9σ$, consistent with the previous measurement. We propose that the two periodic epochs correspond to passages of the magnetar through the decretion disk of the Be-star companion. The captured disk material suppresses low-latitude magnetospheric emission, so that the polar-cap emission dominates and the spin period becomes detectable; alternatively, because the disk material carries substantial angular momentum, accretion increases the magnetic obliquity and thereby amplifies the periodic modulation of the polar-cap emission. The synchronization between the burst periodicity and the magneto-ionic transition points to a link between burst activity and the dynamical evolution of the source environment. The details of the binary-model fit and of the period search are given in Appendices A and B.

papers.title: Bayesian Inference of the Landau Parameter $G'_0$ from Joint Gamow-Teller Measurements
papers.authors: Zidu Lin, Gianluca Colò, A. W. Steiner, Amber Stinson
papers.abstract: $G'_0$ is the leading-order Landau-Migdal parameter that characterizes the spin-isospin dependent nucleon-nucleon interaction. Consequently, the $G'_0$ is closely related to the Gamow-Teller resonance (GTR), the beta and double-beta decay rates of finite nuclei, the response of hot and dense nucleonic matter that modifies the neutrino-nucleon absorption rates in core-collapse supernovae (CCSNe) and binary neutron star (BNS) mergers, and finally the critical density for pion condensation in neutron stars. In this letter, for the first time, we report the $G'_0$ with quantified uncertainty in the framework of Bayesian inference, using a self-consistent standard Skyrme Random Phase Approximation (RPA) model and joint constraints from experimental GTR measurements on $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$, $^{132}\mathrm{Sn}$, $^{90}\mathrm{Zr}$. Our extracted $G_0'$ at saturation density is $0.48\pm0.034$, which is close to the prediction of a few existing Skyrme models that consider spin-isospin observables but smaller than the traditional ones extracted from pion-exchange models. The reasons for this deviation, like the value of the nucleon effective mass $\frac{m^*}{m}$ and the density dependence of $G'_0$, are investigated. The density-dependent $G_0'$ values extracted in this work may guide the construction of new energy density functionals that aims to self-consistently describe the dense matter properties in the spin-isospin channel.

papers.title: An Enhanced Isothermal Jeans Approach to Constraining Dark Matter Self-Interactions from Galactic Kinematics
papers.authors: Zixiang Jia, Fangzhou Jiang, Shubo Li, Ran Li, Jing Wang, Ling Zhu
papers.abstract: We present an improved semi-analytical model to predict density profiles of self-interacting dark matter (SIDM) halos and apply it to constrain the self-scattering cross section using SPARC galaxy rotation curves. Building on the isothermal Jeans approach, our model incorporates (i) velocity-dependent cross sections, (ii) an empirical treatment of core collapse, and (iii) enhanced robustness for identifying solutions. These advances allow us to fit a large sample of galaxies, including systems with baryon-dominated centers often excluded in earlier studies. We find that roughly 1/6 of galaxies admit both a core-growth and a core-collapse solution, while the rest favor a unique evolutionary state. Joint constraints across the sample reveal clear velocity dependence: the allowed parameter space forms an L-shaped degeneracy, where both nearly constant, low cross sections ($σ_0\sim2\,{\rm cm}^2$/g, $ω\gtrsim500\,$km/s) and strongly velocity-dependent models ($σ_0\sim100\,{\rm cm}^2$/g, $ω\sim60\,$km/s) are viable. Adopting the core-growth interpretation yields best-fit values $σ_0\simeq5\,{\rm cm}^2$/g and $ω\simeq250\,$km/s. Our constraints are remarkably consistent with previous results derived from a variety of independent probes. Compared to cold dark matter (CDM) models, SIDM outperforms simple adiabatic-contraction profiles and rivals empirical feedback-based CDM profiles, yet shows no correlation with stellar-to-halo mass ratio, a proxy for feedback strength, offering a distinct explanation for dwarf galaxy diversity. Moreover, SIDM does not affect galaxy-halo scaling relations significantly and makes concentration systematically lower. Our results highlight SIDM as a compelling framework for small-scale structure, while future low-mass kinematic data will be crucial for breaking degeneracies in velocity-dependent cross-section models.

papers.title: Universality of Primordial Anisotropies in Gravitational Wave Background
papers.authors: Boyuan Jiang, Ryo Saito, Ying-li Zhang
papers.abstract: We investigate the general structure of primordial anisotropies in the stochastic gravitational-wave background (SGWB). Many mechanisms generating primordial SGWB anisotropies, including fossil and propagation effects, exhibit similar multipole dependences despite their distinct physical origins, implying the presence of a common underlying structure. To characterize this structure, we introduce a model-independent framework, the Cosmological Form Factor (CFF), that describes how long-wavelength perturbations modulate short-scale SGWB statistics. Within this broad class of mechanisms, we show that the allowed angular and polarization structures of SGWB anisotropies are universally determined by general principles, including statistical isotropy, locality, and the basic properties of long-wavelength perturbations. In contrast to these universal structures, observables such as amplitudes and frequency dependence retain information about the origin. Our results provide a unified and effective description of primordial SGWB anisotropies, clarifying which aspects are universal and which are model dependent, and therefore offer a theoretical foundation for interpreting future gravitational-wave observations.

papers.title: CMB Spectral Distortions from Resonant Conversions in Atomic Dark Sectors
papers.authors: Duncan K. Adams, Jared Barron, Bryce Cyr, Xiuyuan Zhang
papers.abstract: Dark sectors consisting of atomic constituents (electrons, protons, and photons) offer a well-motivated extension to the Standard Model while providing multiple avenues for phenomenological study. In this work, we explore the impact of conversions between the dark and Standard Model photons in the primordial CMB spectral distortion epoch ($10^3 \lesssim z \lesssim 10^6$). These conversions are resonantly enhanced when the induced thermal masses of both photonic species are equal, thus leading to the possibility that sizeable distortions can be produced. To this end, we solve the Boltzmann equation at early times to determine the (irreducible) freeze-in or freeze-out abundance of dark photons. This procedure also allows us to update the limits on generic milli-charged dark sectors using the ACT DR6 bound on the number of effective radiative degrees of freedom ($N_{\rm eff}$). By then modeling the evolution of the thermal masses in both sectors, we compute the primordial CMB distortion using the Landau-Zener formalism. We find that when the dark electron and proton are roughly similar in mass (the positronium limit), current spectral distortion data from the COBE/FIRAS instrument is able to rule out novel regions of parameter space. We also forecast bounds from the proposed FOSSIL satellite, finding that spectral distortions can also be used to probe the ultra-low dark electric charge regions of parameter space, which are difficult to investigate by other means.

papers.title: An efficient finite element formulation for Newtonian noise analysis
papers.authors: Pieter Reumers, Xhorxha Kuci, Stijn François, Geert Degrande
papers.abstract: The Einstein Telescope is a third-generation underground gravitational wave observatory designed to achieve an unprecedented sensitivity down to 3 Hz. Waves propagating in the soil due to anthropogenic or natural vibration sources generate density fluctuations which cause gravitational attraction, resulting in motion of the mirrors of the laser interferometer known as Newtonian noise. A finite element formulation is presented, which evaluates the total Newtonian noise, as well as the bulk and surface contributions, from a seismic wave field defined on a finite element mesh, using Gaussian quadrature. Linear and quadratic tetrahedral (4-node and 10-node) and brick (8-node and 20-node) finite elements are supported. The corresponding volume and surface integrals are expressed in terms of finite element coupling matrices that depend only on the geometry and material properties. The formulation is verified for plane P- and S-waves propagating in an elastic homogeneous full space with a mirror suspended in a spherical cavity, assuming that the wavelength is much larger than the radius of the cavity, so that wave scattering can be ignored. Excellent agreement with analytical solutions is obtained. Similar good agreement is reported for the Newtonian noise on a test mass suspended at a finite distance above the free surface of a homogeneous elastic halfspace in which a Rayleigh wave propagates. The methodology has been implemented in the ANNA Newtonian Noise Analysis toolbox which runs in the MATLAB programming and numeric computing platform and is compatible with the open-source GNU Octave Scientific Programming Language; a Python version is also available. The proposed finite element framework provides a physically consistent and computationally efficient approach for computing gravitational-seismic coupling in heterogeneous media.

papers.title: Dark graviton sensing with magnetically levitated superconductors
papers.authors: Valentina Danieli, Paola C. M. Delgado, Federico R. Urban
papers.abstract: Levitated sensors have emerged as a new frontier to detect ultra-light dark matter such as axion-like particles and dark photons. In this work we study how a magnetically levitated superconductor responds to a spin-2 dark matter field, the dark graviton, in the dHz to kHz frequency range. To do so, we compute the forces that the dark graviton exerts on the superconductor, separately for matter and light couplings. The matter coupling produces a strain-like tidal acceleration between the superconductor and the centre of mass of the rigid apparatus, resulting in a displacement relative to the readout pick-up loop, in a way analogous to the response to a slow, continuous, massive gravitational wave. The light coupling instead induces an effective current that sources an oscillating magnetic field, thus driving the superdiamagnetic response of the superconductor. We find that, albeit with significant experimental improvements, the sensitivity reach for the matter coupling could surpass existing fifth-force experiments in the audio frequency band. At the same time, magnetically levitated superconductors could be among the most sensitive laboratory probes of the dark-graviton coupling to electromagnetism, especially at low frequencies, provided technical and readout noise can be kept under control.

papers.title: Particle--antiparticle asymmetry from charge separation at expanding horizons
papers.authors: She-Sheng Xue
papers.abstract: In a Friedmann universe with a time-varying cosmological term, massive particle--antiparticle pairs are produced continuously from the spacetime vacuum, and their members are separated by horizons. Along the cosmic history that explains $n_s$, $A_s$, $r$ and the low-$\ell$ power anomaly, we show how this separation generates the observed asymmetry. Horizons absorb the charge they separate, since gravity does not conserve global charges. Charge separation at the many horizons inside today's Hubble volume then acts as a volume violation of the U(1) charge, at a rate $Γ_C=κ_CΓ_M$ proportional to pair production. The sign requires a C- and CP-odd coupling to the time arrow. We describe both by an effective Lagrangian with a U(1)-violating coupling $g_c\,δ\mathcal O_SΦ^2$ to the spacetime vacuum and a time bias $-\partial_μf(R)\,J^μ$. For $f=c_a\ln|R|$ the chemical potential of producing a particle is $μ\simeq2c_a\dot H/H$. The asymmetry per pair reaches an attractor in the pair-dominated episode and freezes when the cosmological term is exhausted. The observed value requires $|c_a|/τ_S\simeq(0.65$--$1.0)\times10^{-4}$, with $T_S=τ_SH/2π$ the temperature of the spacetime vacuum, and its sign is fixed by the arrow of time. The Yukawa decays of the pairs transfer the asymmetry, with a uniform sign, to baryons and leptons and to dark-matter particles. The current of the charged decay products generates a magnetic field of $10^{-14}$--$10^{-11}$ G today on the coherence length of reheating.

papers.title: Small-Scale Dynamo for Full Spectrum of Hydrodynamic Turbulence in Kazantsev Model
papers.authors: Leonid Kitchatinov
papers.abstract: A method is proposed for computing coefficients in the Kazantsev equation of small-scale dynamo for the full spectrum of hydromagnetic turbulence comprising the inertial range together with the range of viscous dissipation. The dynamo equation with so-defined coefficients is solved numerically for magnetic (Rm) and hydrodynamic (Re) Reynolds numbers from $10^2$ to $10^8$. The threshold value ${\rm Rm}_c$ for onset of dynamo increases initially with Re but then saturates at a constant value of ${\rm Rm}_c \simeq 300$ for ${\rm Re}\geq 10^5$. In the case of small Prandtl number Pm = Rm/Re << 1, the field growth rate is also small and depends logarithmically on Rm. In this case, the magnetic energy spectrum peaks around the scale of Ohmic dissipation, which decreases with increasing Pm. The decrease stops at the scale of viscous dissipation while the growth rate increases sharply when Pm approaches the value of one. The increase in the growth rate proceeds to ${\rm Pm} > 1$ but slows down and then saturates at a value somewhat below the inverse lifetime of most short-living eddies. An explanation of the results is proposed.

papers.title: Neutrino transport and flavor instabilities in a post-merger disk
papers.authors: Erick Urquilla, Swapnil Shankar, Debraj Kundu, Julien Froustey, Sherwood Richers, Jonah M. Miller, Gail C. McLaughlin, James P. Kneller, Francois Foucart
papers.abstract: Neutron star mergers are multimessenger sources whose dynamics and signals depend critically on neutrinos and their flavor transformations. We investigate whether fast and collisional neutrino flavor instabilities (FFIs and CFIs) arise in a GW170817-like post-merger accretion disk using the six-dimensional phase-space particle-in-cell transport code \texttt{EMU}. In the accretion disk, the neutrino radiation field naturally develops electron-lepton-number crossings through the interplay between the more isotropic electron-neutrino field and the more anisotropic electron-antineutrino field. The disk's neutrino field is also unstable to CFI, though on longer timescales than FFI. We study how instabilities relax by performing quantum-kinetic simulations in centimeter-wide domains with periodic boundary conditions at selected points. We find that the isolated effects of FFI and CFI increase the heavy-lepton neutrino fluxes. CFI breaks the initial symmetry of the heavy-flavor sector by raising the average energy of heavy-flavor antineutrinos above that of heavy-flavor neutrinos. We perform global quantum-kinetic simulations using a Hamiltonian attenuated by factors between $10^{-12}$ and $10^{-5}$. Although we resolve unstable flavor waves, attenuation increases the instability growth timescale by orders of magnitude relative to the advection timescale; therefore, neutrinos leave the domain before FFI and CFI can saturate. The in-medium effective mixing angles and mass splittings, driven by the combined vacuum, matter, and neutrino-neutrino potentials, then govern the quantum-kinetic evolution. These results highlight the resolution and scaling requirements for future global simulations that capture instability growth, saturation, and advection simultaneously.

papers.title: Cosmology of Inelastic Self-Interacting Dark Matter: Linear Evolution and Observational Constraints
papers.authors: Xin-Chen Duan, Yue-Lin Sming Tsai, Ziwei Wang
papers.abstract: We study the linear cosmological evolution of inelastic self-interacting dark matter in a two-component dark sector with a small mass splitting, assuming thermal initial conditions for the two species. We derive the coupled background and perturbation equations for inelastic conversion between the two species, considering both power-law and low-velocity saturation cross sections. Exothermic conversion injects kinetic energy into the light component, generating pressure support that suppresses small-scale structure and produces dark acoustic oscillations in the matter power spectrum. The resulting cutoff at scale $k > 1\,h\,\mathrm{Mpc}^{-1}$ depends on the normalization and velocity dependence of the cross section, the dark matter mass and the mass splitting. Using linear power spectra computed with a modified Boltzmann solver, we apply recast constraints from Lyman-$α$ forest data and high-redshift UV luminosity functions, finding non-monotonic but closed exclusion regions driven by the competition between efficient conversion and rapid depletion of the heavy component. These results show that the internal thermodynamics of a secluded multi-component dark sector can leave observable imprints on structure formation, providing a complementary probe of secluded dark matter.

papers.title: Parity-dependent wave absorption and optical characteristics of a cored magnetic black hole
papers.authors: Mohsen Fathi, Faizuddin Ahmed
papers.abstract: We study light propagation and coupled gravitational--electromagnetic waves around a black hole supported by a nonlinear magnetic field. The same field action fixes the geometry, the mass--charge relation, and the wave potentials. We calculate two critical impact parameters for light and solve the coupled scattering equations in both parity sectors. In eight solutions of one action, the two optical scales differ by $3.6$--$7.2\%$. The wave absorption also depends on parity. For $\ell=2$, the gap between the larger absorption eigenvalues reaches about $9.0$ percentage points. A wider frequency scan reveals a stronger effect in the second eigenchannel. The difference between the two absorption traces reaches $24.3$ percentage points. The trace equals twice the absorption of an equal incoherent mixture of incoming gravitational and electromagnetic fields. A controlled test of the wave operator shows that the nonlinear electromagnetic factor $κ$ plays an important role in the parity gap. We also examine four $\ell=3$ cases and use charge-matched Reissner--Nordström black holes as a separate control. The optical and wave calculations provide two complementary properties of the same magnetic source.

papers.title: Eigenvalue formulation of Stochastic Inflation and application to large perturbation generating inflationary features
papers.authors: Swagat S. Mishra, Edmund J. Copeland, Anne M. Green
papers.abstract: Stochastic inflation is a powerful technique for calculating the probability distribution function (PDF) of large inflationary perturbations, which may collapse to form Primordial Black Holes. The PDF, $P({\cal N})$, of the stochastic number of e-folds, ${\cal N}$, satisfies an adjoint Fokker-Planck Equation. We develop a new self-contained eigenvalue technique which can be used to determine $P({\cal N})$. First we apply this method to the simple case of quantum diffusion along a flat potential without any classical drift. We recover the expression for the PDF that has previously been found using characteristic functions, with an exponential tail, and a power-law behaviour, $P({\cal N}) \propto {\cal N}^{-3/2}$, in the intermediate regime between the peak and the tail of the PDF. Finally we apply the method to constant drift inflation, in the narrow- and broad-well limits. In the narrow-well limit, there is an analytic solution and the PDF is similar to the drift-free case, with a mildly suppressed tail. In the broad-well limit, determining the full set of eigenvalues and eigenfunctions requires a piecewise construction of the spectrum, and the broad-well PDF is qualitatively different, with an enhanced peak and a strongly suppressed tail.

papers.title: SDSS-V LVM: Revealing the Physical and Chemical Structure of the Helix Nebula
papers.authors: R. Orozco-Duarte, J. E. Méndez-Delgado, J. A. Toalá, L. Sabin, C. Morisset, S. F. Sánchez, H. Ibarra-Medel, W. J. Henney, A. Z. Lugo-Aranda, A. Singh, E. J. Johnston, A. Roman-Lopes, C. G. Román-Zúñiga, I. Cruz-Gonzalez, Guy S. Stringfellow, M. Peña, A. Wofford, E. Egorova, O. Aranguré, L. C. Castañeda-Carlos, S. Torres-Peimbert, L. Hernández-Martínez, J. R. Brownstein, R. de J. Zermeño, I. Yu. Katkov, Oleg V. Egorov, A. J. Mejía-Narváez, G. A. Blanc, Mónica, A. Villa-Durango
papers.abstract: We present the first spatially contiguous study of the physical and chemical structure of the Helix Nebula (NGC~7293, PNG 036.1-57.1) based on integral-field spectroscopy from the SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM). The wide-field observations provide nearly complete spectroscopic coverage of the nebula, enabling a spaxel-by-spaxel analysis of extinction, electron density and temperature, ionisation structure, and chemical abundances. We reconstruct calibrated datacubes from the LVM row-stacked spectra and measure 41 optical emission lines, including hydrogen, helium, and collisionally excited metal lines. The resulting maps reveal a strongly stratified nebula, with highly ionised gas traced by \heii~concentrated toward the central cavity, low-ionisation material dominating the bright shell, and neutral or transition-zone gas enhanced in the outer regions. The Helix is a low-density object, with typical electron densities of $\sim10^{2}\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, and exhibits a non-uniform temperature structure, with variations of several thousand Kelvin across different ionisation zones. We derive a near-solar oxygen abundance, $12+\log(\mathrm{O/H})\simeq8.7$, consistent with spatially complete sampling. The central abundance pattern indicates a significant contribution from unobserved O$^{3+}$, suggesting that apparent abundance variations are primarily driven by ionisation effects rather than true chemical inhomogeneities. We also find evidence for a sulfur deficit of $\sim$1 dex, consistent with the planetary-nebula sulfur anomaly. The helium and nitrogen abundances place the Helix near the classical boundary of Type~I planetary nebulae, suggesting moderate chemical enrichment by its progenitor star.

papers.title: Are neutrinos Majorana? Fixed-target and high-energy astrophysical searches decide
papers.authors: Gabriela Barenboim, Mauricio Bustamante, Qinrui Liu
papers.abstract: The original version of this paper proposed a new approach to determining whether neutrinos are Dirac or Majorana fermions, a fundamental open question in particle physics. Conventional searches rely on neutrinoless double beta decay, but this electron-only channel suffers from blind spots. We propose a new, complementary probe to overcome this limitation. A heavy neutral lepton (HNL) triggers a high-energy shift in how the active neutrino flavors ($ν_e$, $ν_μ$, $ν_τ$) mix---but only if the neutrinos are Majorana. For GeV-scale HNLs, the upcoming beam-dump experiment SHiP can discover the HNL and measure how it mixes with the active flavors.However, the proposed signature of the Majorana nature of neutrinos does not exist. The reasons are explained here. The analysis has been superseded by Ref.~\cite{Barenboim:2026udr}. The original version is retained as v1 for the record.

papers.title: Memoirs of the curvaton: non-perturbative non-Gaussianity and supermassive primordial black holes
papers.authors: S. Allegrini, A. J. Iovino, G. Perna, H. Veermäe
papers.abstract: The curvaton provides a simple mechanism for generating strongly non-Gaussian curvature perturbations after inflation, with potentially important consequences on small scales. We study curvaton dynamics beyond the standard quadratic potential and construct the local non-Gaussian map $ζ=F(ζ_{\rm G})$ relating the curvature perturbation to an auxiliary Gaussian field $ζ_{\rm G}$. Curvaton self-interactions make the onset of oscillations field dependent and modify the effective equation of state once the curvaton enters the adiabatic regime. We incorporate these effects using the abbreviated action, which provides a compact way to connect the frozen and oscillatory regimes and exposes sources of non-Gaussianity absent in the purely quadratic case. We apply the formalism to quadratic, monomial, quartic, and cosine potentials, for which we derive the mapping $F(ζ_{\rm G})$ and show that self-interactions can either enhance or suppress the resulting non-Gaussianity depending on the potential and initial conditions. We consider non-perturbative aspects in the strongly non-Gaussian regime, and show how strong non-Gaussianity can suppress the power spectrum. As an application, we provide a bottom-up scenario in which strongly positive curvaton non-Gaussianity allows primordial supermassive black hole seeds at peak amplitudes $\mathcal{A}_\textrm{pk}\sim10^{-3}$, which are compatible with the COBE/FIRAS $μ$-distortion bounds. This opens a new primordial scenario for the Little Red Dots observed by the JWST. The axion-like curvaton provides a particularly natural setting for this mechanism.

papers.title: Landau-Zener formula and resonant axion conversion in neutron star magnetospheres
papers.authors: Matti Heikinheimo, Topi Sirkiä, Kimmo Tuominen
papers.abstract: We investigate the Landau-Zener description of resonant axion-photon conversion in neutron star magnetospheres. We find that this picture often fails for axion conversions to millimeter-to-optical band photons due to the characteristic resonance width exceeding the size of the conversion region. This comparison of scales yields a simple criterion for evaluating the validity of the Landau-Zener formula. We verify this criterion numerically, and show that when invalid, the Landau-Zener conversion probability may significantly deviate from the numerical result. In light of these findings, we revise constraints on axions from neutron star optical-band polarization searches.

papers.title: Odd-parity ringdown gravitational waves of a spherically symmetric black hole with perfect fluid accretion
papers.authors: Rikuto Ohashi, Yasutaka Koga, Hiroyuki Nakano, Kota Ogasawara, Chul-Moon Yoo
papers.abstract: The ringdown waves from a black hole offer a clean probe of strong-field gravity, but a matter distribution that may be present around a realistic black hole renders the background spacetime dynamical and the ringdown frequencies time-dependent. We study the odd-parity ringdown of a Schwarzschild black hole that grows through the dilute, steady, spherically symmetric accretion of a perfect fluid. Working to first order in the accretion rate, we compute the ringdown waveform directly in the time domain on this dynamical background. Since the odd-parity matter perturbation decouples from the metric perturbation, the wave mode can be described by a purely tensorial mode on the accreting background. In particular, the ratio of the imaginary to the real part of the frequency cancels both the secular variation caused by the growth of the black hole and the redshift factor, so that its deviation from the Schwarzschild value purely reflects the surrounding environment. The time dependence of the frequency, on the other hand, reflects the accretion rate and allows us to define a second observable tied to it. We argue that measuring these observables across multiple modes may provide significant information to constrain the surrounding environment of the black hole.

papers.title: Infrared spectroscopy of gas-phase hydrogenated and methylated pyrenes: from laboratory spectra to the simulated 3.4 $μ$m emission band
papers.authors: Karine Demyk, Christine Joblin, Louan de Bentzmann, Dominique Toublanc, Giacomo Mulas
papers.abstract: Observations of the aromatic infrared emission band at 3.3 mic often reveal satellite emission features in the 3.4 - 3.6 mic range. While the 3.3 mic band is attributed to the CH stretching vibration of polycylic aromatic hydrocarbons (PAHs), the satellite bands - particularly its prominent 3.4 mic component - is assigned to aliphatic CH stretching vibrations in hydrogenated and methylated PAH-like species. Our aim is to derive state-of-the-art infrared emission spectra for aliphatic-containing pyrene derivatives and compare them with astronomical observations. This will help refine our understanding of the contribution of these species to the 3.4 mic emission band. Mid-infrared spectra (1.4-25 mic of gas-phase dihydropyrene, tehtrahydropyrene, hexahydropyrene methylated pyrene, and pyrene were recorded at temperatures ranging from 373 to 673 K, depending on the species. The band profiles were analyzed using a multi-component fitting tool, and empirical anharmonicity laws were derived to quantify the evolution of the band positions and widths with temperature. The obtained spectral data was combined with the results of a Monte Carlo emission model to simulate the emission spectra following UV-photon absorption, up to the dissociation limit (<6 eV). The resulting synthetic spectra were compared with James Webb Space Telescope observations of the Orion Bar region (PDRs4All program). Based on these state-of-the-art simulated spectra, we show that 1,2,3,6,7,8-hexahydropyrene matches all the constrains to fit the red component of the 3.4 mic band observed at 3.403 mic. While 1-methylpyrene may also contribute to the underlying emission plateau, its lack of a strong infrared band complicates detection in observed spectra, unlike hexahydropyrene. All experimental spectra and their temperature-dependent analyses are available in the new cosmicPAH-IRDB database.

papers.title: Eccentricity as a Magnifying Glass: Precision Population Inference Enabled by Eccentric Neutron Star-Black Hole Mergers
papers.authors: Alberto Salvarese, Hsin-Yu Chen, Aaron Zimmerman, Snehal Tibrewal
papers.abstract: The formation history of compact binary systems remains one of the key open questions in astrophysics. Theoretical studies generally favor isolated binary evolution for neutron star-black hole (NSBH) systems, which tends to produce nearly circular orbits. However, recent analyses of the gravitational-wave event GW200105 indicate that its source has measurable eccentricity, suggesting that alternative formation channels may also contribute. It has been shown that the intrinsic parameters of eccentric NSBH mergers, such as the component masses and spins, are much better measured than circular mergers with LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) observatories. We explore how such eccentricity-enhanced parameter measurements can affect the inference of NSBH formation channels. We find that sharper measurements of the effective spin parameter $χ_{\rm eff}$ increase the fraction of systems for which negative values can be confidently identified, allowing for the clear measurement of a spin-orbit misaligned event every $\sim 2.5$ eccentric NSBH detections for an isotropically distributed population in the fifth LVK observing run (O5). Improved neutron star (NS) mass measurements provide better constraining power for NS mass distributions, potentially revealing structure and tightening the bounds that can be drawn on their upper and lower masses. Similarly, the recovery of a metallicity-dependent BH mass distribution is improved by eccentricity-enhanced measurements. Finally, we show that the proposed population-level eccentricity distribution for dynamical-formation channels can be tested by the end of O5.

papers.title: Revealing a multi-zone circumnuclear dust response in UGC 11487 through phase-resolved WISE W1--W2 diagnostics
papers.authors: I. O. Izviekova, O. V. Kompaniiets, I. B. Vavilova, D. V. Dobrycheva
papers.abstract: Mid-infrared (MIR) flares provide a direct probe of dust reprocessing in obscured tidal disruption event (TDE) candidates when the primary optical or ultraviolet flare is weak, missed, or strongly attenuated. We present a phase-resolved analysis of the WISE/NEOWISE W1-W2 evolution of the MIR-selected TDE candidate UGC 11487/WTP14adeqka over 2014-2024. We combine timing, colour, and flux diagnostics with phenomenological modelling, hydrodynamically motivated clumpy dust-echo calculations, and an aperture-matched ultraviolet-to-radio spectral energy distribution of the host. The decade-long flare shows a delayed and broader W2 response, colour hysteresis, and cooling from approximately 900 K to 500-600 K. Positive-fluence centroids yield a preferred delay of $224 +/- 45$ d, corresponding to $0.188 +/- 0.038$ pc. The effective infrared luminosity peaks at approximately $3 x 10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, and the integrated infrared energy is $(2.9-3.8) x 10^{51}$ erg. A single self-similar MIR response is strongly disfavoured, with Delta BIC = 281.7, while the preferred compact description is a two-component phenomenological model. Representative hydro-clumpy calculations reproduce the empirical diagnostics in a structured, multi-zone dust-response scenario. The host is a moderately star-forming isolated barred disc without a dominant persistent active galactic nucleus component. These results support an obscured TDE-like accretion transient reprocessed by structured circumnuclear dust and show that phase-resolved WISE diagnostics can recover characteristic sub-parsec response scales in obscured accretion-powered nuclear transients.

papers.title: Unsupervised selection and characterisation of little red dots in JWST surveys with manifold learning
papers.authors: Michele Ginolfi, Filippo Mannucci, Alessandro Marconi, Francesco D'Eugenio, Giacomo Venturi, Francesco Belfiore, Giovanni Cresci, Caterina Bracci, Stefano Carniani, Alessandra Cozzi, Roberto Maiolino, Guido Risaliti
papers.abstract: Little red dots (LRDs) are compact, red sources discovered at high redshifts by JWST, and their physical nature and selection function remain a topic of debate. Here, we investigate whether an unsupervised machine-learning approach applied to multi-band photometry has the capacity to identify LRD-like objects, along with other populations, without relying on predefined colour-cuts. Using UMAP, a manifold-learning (dimensionality-reduction) method, we placed ~242,000 isolated, well-measured sources from the ASTRODEEP-JWST catalogue on a 2D map, where objects with similar broadband colours, morphology, and photometric redshift lie close together. We then used spectroscopically confirmed LRDs to identify where LRD-like objects lie within this map. We compared the resulting areas with published colour cuts and validated our data-driven selection against archival NIRSpec spectra from the DJA. We find that the spectroscopically selected LRDs are concentrated in two well-defined regions with no colour-cut imposed, tracing populations that differ mainly in redshift; a difference that is imprinted on their broadband colours. The main region reaches a purity of ~0.78 at ~0.82 completeness on the spectroscopically classified subset. This result is competitive with (or cleaner than) literature colour-cuts, and yields ~100 additional candidates. We also tested the method as a general tool for population discovery: the manifold recovers the locations of brown dwarfs and broad-line active galactic nuclei with no explicit criterion and isolates rare pathological outliers. Overall, unsupervised manifolds, anchored by sparse high-confidence spectroscopic labels, provide an efficient, assumption-light framework for characterising populations, comparing selection methods on a common basis, and discovering rare objects in large photometric datasets.

papers.title: Gravitational waves from super-Hubble bubbles
papers.authors: Pulkit S. Ghoderao, Arttu Rajantie, Danièle Steer
papers.abstract: We consider a cosmological first-order phase transition in which bubbles of true vacuum nucleate during inflation but do not collide and percolate until the Universe has entered the radiation-dominated era. If the collisions take place soon after the end of inflation, the size of these bubbles can be significantly greater than the Hubble length. This has two important consequences for the gravitational waves produced by the bubble collisions: First, as the peak frequency is determined by the comoving bubble radius, it can be well below the MHz frequencies typical for bubble collisions at the end of inflation. Second, when comparing collisions beginning at the same time, the amplitude of the gravitational waves is greatly enhanced relative to Hubble-sized and smaller bubbles. Together, these two effects mean that gravitational waves produced by super-Hubble bubbles soon after the end of inflation can be within the observable frequency and amplitude ranges of LIGO and NANOGrav, as well as LISA and other future gravitational wave experiments. We demonstrate this with a simple illustrative model.

papers.title: How to raise a supermassive black hole: interpreting early JWST AGN with the AESOPICA simulations
papers.authors: Sophie Koudmani, Jan Scholtz, Anthony J. Taylor, Ignas Juodžbalis, Debora Sijacki, Rachel S. Somerville, Roberto Maiolino, Emma Curtis-Lake, Steven L. Finkelstein, Martin A. Bourne, Francesco D'Eugenio, Sophia Geris, Lucy R. Ivey, Hannah Übler
papers.abstract: The active galactic nuclei (AGN) uncovered by JWST in the early Universe are highly abundant and seemingly overmassive with respect to local scaling relations, challenging standard models of black hole formation and growth. Yet it remains unclear whether they trace an efficient early growth channel, represent the observable tail of a broader population, or reflect systematic uncertainties in mass estimates. We introduce the AESOPICA project, a suite of twelve mid-volume ($L = 60\,\mathrm{cMpc}$) cosmological simulations based on the FABLE galaxy formation model, varying the black hole seed mass across the theoretical formation channels ($M_\mathrm{seed} = 10^{2}$-$10^{5} \,\mathrm{M_{\odot}}$), the accretion efficiency, including super-Eddington bursts, and the supernova feedback strength. We forward-model observational selection with BALMERSOPICA, a mock JWST broad-line survey pipeline that assesses the detectability of each simulated AGN for a given grating and exposure time. We find that the bulk of the JWST AGN population can be assembled from any seed mass provided the accretion efficiency is high, although light seeds require the most favourable accretion conditions explored. Applying broad-line selection naturally recovers the apparently overmassive population, with the detected AGN lying furthest above the intrinsic $M_\mathrm{BH}$-$M_\mathrm{stellar}$ relation for inefficient accretion models. The selected AGN lie on the local, weakly evolving $M_\mathrm{BH}$-$σ_\mathrm{stellar}$ relation, supporting a scenario where black holes assemble before the stellar component is fully established. Since efficient accretion rapidly erases the imprint of the initial seed mass, the low-mass end of the black hole mass function and host gas-phase metallicities offer the most promising discriminants between seeding channels.

papers.title: Sample Variance Cancellation for Future Spectroscopic Surveys
papers.authors: James M. Sullivan, Martin White
papers.abstract: High-redshift spectroscopic galaxy surveys will be the scientific engines of the next generation of large-scale structure cosmology. The clustering signal of high redshift, star-forming Lyman-$α$ emitters (LAEs) will be of key importance for obtaining high-redshift constraints on the growth of structure and redshift-space distortions. The complex radiative transfer (RT) of Lyman-$α$ photons alters the symmetry group respected by the overdensity field constructed from these galaxies, and so the observed large-scale clustering of LAEs may have an angular dependence that differs significantly from that of linear theory, possibly biasing inference of cosmological parameters. While such an effect has been seen in simulations, its amplitude in nature and its detailed form remains unclear. In the restricted context of a linear, Gaussian model, we outline a procedure for pinning down the type and amplitude of such changes in angular dependence on large scales due to unknown RT or a more general unmodeled angular effect in the hypothetical scenario in which an observer is presented with LAE data containing such an effect. We show that if a second tracer without the modified angular dependence is available for cross correlation with the LAEs at the same redshifts (e.g., Lyman-break galaxies), then, with a high redshift survey of modest size, it is possible to rapidly identify: 1) the presence of a nontrivial angular functional form of radiative transfer (by a conditional field-level realization), 2) the functional form itself (with an optimal filter that we derive), and 3) the value of its amplitude with an uncertainty (via an adaptation of the standard quadratic estimator). Such sample-variance-cancellation strategies therefore provide a statistical solution to unknown astrophysical or systematic angular clustering dependence, including from RT.

papers.title: Reconnection-driven Plasma Loading for Prompt Emission in Tidal Disruption Event Jets
papers.authors: Rin Oikawa, Yuri Sato
papers.abstract: A tidal disruption event (TDE) occurs when a star passes sufficiently close to a black hole (BH) to be disrupted by its tidal forces. Although several hundred TDEs have been identified to date, only a small fraction launch relativistic jets. These jets are thought to be Poynting-flux-dominated outflows powered by the Blandford-Znajek (BZ) mechanism. However, the origin of the jet plasma required to account for the observed prompt emission remains poorly understood and constitutes a key unresolved problem in the formation of relativistic TDE jets. In this Letter, we propose magnetic reconnection near the BH as a physical mechanism for injecting plasma into the BZ jet during the super-Eddington accretion phase. Once sufficient magnetic flux accumulates near the BH, an equatorial current sheet forms, in which magnetic reconnection produces high-energy gamma rays. We demonstrate that photon-photon interactions generate a sufficient particle supply to account for the observed prompt emission. We further show that our plasma loading scenario allows the jet to remain magnetically dominated out to the prompt emission region and that magnetic dissipation can consistently reproduce the observed prompt emission properties. Furthermore, our scenario predicts MeV and GeV gamma-ray flares, providing a direct means of testing this scenario with future gamma-ray observatories.

papers.title: Multipolar neutrino radiation in binary neutron star mergers: Angular structure, rotational variability, and implications for electron fraction
papers.authors: Kutay Arınç Çokluk, Albino Perego, Federico Maria Guercilena, Kadri Yakut
papers.abstract: The angular structure and temporal variability of neutrino emission from binary neutron star mergers are characterized using fully general-relativistic simulations with energy-integrated M1 neutrino transport across a representative set of equations of state, total masses and mass ratios. The main analysis is restricted to merger remnants that do not collapse to a black hole within the simulated time intervals. The angle-dependent neutrino energy flux is extracted on a spherical surface outside the remnant and decomposed into spherical harmonics to quantify its multipolar content and evolution. Following the initial post-merger transient, the neutrino radiation flux approaches an axisymmetric configuration dominated by a strong quadrupolar component, producing persistent polar flux enhancement and equatorial suppression due to torus shadowing. The dipolar contribution remains subdominant, indicating the absence of sustained one-sided emission. The degree of anisotropy increases with mass asymmetry and for softer equations of state, reflecting the compactness and morphology of the remnant--disk system. Superimposed on this time-averaged geometry, coherent azimuthal modulations associated with the $m=1$ mode are identified. The associated half frequency, $f_{\mathrm{dom}}/2\simeq0.6$--$0.7\,\mathrm{kHz}$, is compared with local rotation rates in the simulated remnant--disk systems, suggesting a possible dynamical association between the remnant structure and neutrino variability. Finally, we quantify how the same quadrupole-dominated radiation geometry induces a latitude-dependent equilibrium electron fraction. The polar material is driven close to the neutrino-equilibrium target, whereas equatorial material remains systematically more neutron rich and below equilibrium.

papers.title: Calibration of CNEOS Fireball Velocities and the Robustness of Nominally Hyperbolic Events
papers.authors: Volkan Duran, Abraham Loeb
papers.abstract: The NASA/JPL CNEOS Fireball Data catalogue provides a near-global record of bright atmospheric entries but does not report per-event velocity covariance. We calibrate its kinematic accuracy using 19 events with independent reference trajectories and use optical, satellite, radar, and infrasound catalogues as source-specific controls. For nine modern high-quality comparisons, the CNEOS-minus-reference speed residual has mean -1.00 km s$^{-1}$ and standard deviation 0.86 km s$^{-1}$; variance decomposition assigns 0.77 km s$^{-1}$ to the CNEOS component. The radiant residuals have a 0.74 degree per-axis core plus one 16.3 degree outlier, so the extreme tail remains poorly determined. Seven of 354 complete CNEOS states are nominally hyperbolic without correction. A +0.9935 km s$^{-1}$ atmospheric-stage shift produces five additional crossings, but these are treated only as sensitivity cases. Polar-IM (2026 April 1) is the strongest post-2018 CNEOS anomaly, whereas independent GLM-LI stereo solutions yield 57.3 +/- 2.0 and 56.7 +/- 3.0 km s$^{-1}$, close to their direction-specific parabolic thresholds. We conclude that CNEOS can identify priority candidates, but secure interstellar classification requires an independent, uncertainty-bearing three-dimensional trajectory for the same event.

papers.title: A Novel Approach to 3D Dust Mapping of the Central Molecular Zone
papers.authors: Arianna Vasini, Mattia C. Sormani, Jason L. Sanders, Adam Ginsburg, Cara Battersby, Francisco Nogueras-Lara, Rainer Schödel, Evangelia Deliporanidou, Marco Donati, Zi-Xuan Feng, Karl Fiteni, Savannah Gramze, Xingchen Li, Dani R. Lipman, Perry H. Hatchfield
papers.abstract: The 3D distribution of dust and gas in the Milky Way's Central Molecular Zone (CMZ) is key to understanding gas inflows towards the Galactic Centre (GC), the process of star formation in this extreme environment, and the propagation of energetic cosmic rays originating from Sgr A*. However, while recent efforts have combined datasets in a Bayesian framework to estimate the near/far positions of individual molecular clouds in the CMZ, conflicts between different methodologies still remain and we are still lacking a comprehensive, model-independent map of all of the gas and dust in the CMZ, which is critical to address key science questions. Here we develop a new methodology to infer the 3D dust distribution of the CMZ. The key idea of the method is to use stellar proper motions to get probabilistic information about the unknown stellar distances through a model of the distribution of star positions and velocities of the nuclear stellar disc (NSD), co-spatial with the CMZ. Taking stellar proper motions and extinctions as input, the latter adopted as a proxy of the dust column density, the method returns the 3D dust distribution. It is non-parametric, makes no assumptions on the functional form of the dust distribution, and is fundamentally distinct and largely independent of all existing methods. We show that the method can robustly and effectively reconstruct the mock 3D CMZ structure by testing it on a range of mock dust distributions, both analytically generated and taken from hydrodynamical simulations. Finally, we discuss the prospects for applying the method to real data.

papers.title: Relativistic hydrodynamics of a charged fluid from Myers-Pospelov Lorentz-Violating Electrodynamics
papers.authors: Matheus Duarte, Vitor de Souza
papers.abstract: We derive the equations of relativistic hydrodynamics for a charged fluid from Lorentz-violating Myers--Pospelov electrodynamics. Starting from the modified fermionic and electromagnetic equations of motion, we employ the covariant Wigner formalism to establish the semiclassical spectral constraints and distribution function, which, combined with Noether's theorem, yield the energy-momentum tensor, particle current, and corresponding conservation laws in the presence of Lorentz violation. The resulting hydrodynamic description contains Lorentz-violating corrections to the thermodynamic quantities and to the fluid currents. In the purely timelike sector, these corrections can be absorbed into effective thermodynamic quantities, preserving the isotropic structure of the fluid equations. In contrast, spacelike backgrounds introduce explicit contributions along the preferred direction, which cannot be absorbed into the standard hydrodynamic variables and give rise to anisotropic forces and torques. These effects lead to departures from standard relativistic charged-fluid hydrodynamics and provide a direct macroscopic manifestation of the Lorentz-violating background. Our results establish a first-principles framework for investigating the macroscopic consequences of Lorentz violation in relativistic charged fluids and provide a starting point for the development of a consistent Lorentz-violating relativistic magnetohydrodynamic theory.

papers.title: Medium effects on neutron star modified and direct Urca cooling rates
papers.authors: B. X. Zhou, Jin-Biao Wei, Z. H. Li, G. F. Burgio, H. -J. Schulze
papers.abstract: We study the effects of in-medium modification of the elementary cooling processes on observable properties of isolated neutron stars. We then deduce the neutron star mass distributions compatible with the cooling analysis and compare with current theoretical models. We conclude that current cooling data require fast direct Urca (DU) cooling, moderated by proton superfluidity, to be active in most neutron stars, and that the DU onset threshold must lie below canonical masses. In that case medium modifications of modified Urca (MU) rates are practically insignificant, but the $nn$ Bremsstrahlung rate plays a dominant role.

papers.title: Geometrical and Optical Design of the GUEST Laser-Ranged Test Masses for the Detection of Gravitational Waves in the $μ$Hz range
papers.authors: Dario Vetrano, Giada Bargiacchi, Nicolò Burzillà, Roberto Campagnola, Francesco Del Ferraro Iacobelli, Luca Porcelli, Simone Dell'Agnello, Diego Blas
papers.abstract: The GUEST (Gravitational Universe Exploration with Satellite Tracking) mission aims at detecting gravitational waves in the yet almost unexplored $μ$Hz frequency range through high-precision orbital tracking. The unprecedented scientific objectives of this experiment demand equally advanced optical solutions: the highly eccentric orbit imposes dual measurement regimes; a low-velocity, long-range scenario at apogee and a high-velocity, short-range scenario at perigee. The substantial disparity between these conditions is addressed through a novel optical architecture incorporating two distinct types of Corner-Cube Retroreflectors (CCRs) with 1" and 2" apertures (CCR1 and CCR2, respectively). The proposed layout has been designed to ensure isotropy and homogeneity of the optical response while maintaining efficient packing over the spherical surface of the spacecraft. The resulting Optical Cross-Section (OCS) has been evaluated using a custom reduced-order model, which captures the behavior of individual CCRs under varying illumination conditions. This model has been calibrated by reconstructing the optical response of the LARES-2 satellite and has enabled a detailed assessment of the contributions of each CCR type along the GUEST orbit. Finally, sensitivity analyses have been conducted to investigate the impact of key design parameters, including the ratio between CCR types, laser wavelength, spacecraft diameter, Dihedral Angle Offsets (DAOs), and mechanical configurations.

papers.title: Multiwavelength Classification of Chandra Sources in Omega Centauri
papers.authors: Steven Chen, Oleg Kargaltsev, Jeremy Hare, Hui Yang, Oleg Smirnov, Ian Heywood, Talon Myburgh
papers.abstract: We present a comprehensive study of X-ray sources in the globular cluster NGC 5139 to date. Over 200 Chandra sources are cross-matched to multiwavelength catalogs from HST, JWST, and MeerKAT. We employ a machine-learning classification pipeline (MUWCLASS) for the first time in such a crowded stellar environment and introduce the globular-cluster-specific training dataset, which compiles previously classified sources from 25 Galactic globular clusters. Given the challenges presented by the high-density environment, we compare the MUWCLASS results with traditional classification methods. We confirm counterpart associations suggested in previous works and also identify new confident and candidate associations. We discuss the implications of our classification results in light of models of cluster dynamical evolution and binary formation/destruction.

papers.title: The origin and distribution of diffuse HI in the close interacting MHONGOOSE galaxy systems
papers.authors: D. Kleiner, W. J. G. de Blok, J. Healy, F. M. Maccagni, E. M. Di Teodoro, A. Fraser-McKelvie, A. Marasco, S. Veronese, S. Kurapati
papers.abstract: We present the deepest HI observations of the two systems with Dproj < 100 kpc, and $Δ$ vsys < 200 km/s in the MHONGOOSE survey. The MeerKAT observations are characterised by 3$σ$ NHI = 10$^{17.9}$ cm$^{-2}$ over 16 km/s at 4 kpc scales. The new data have enabled us to detect HI in seven galaxies: the interacting NGC 3511/3513 pair, and an interacting triplet (NGC 4781, NGC 4790 and UGCA 308) along with two new (2MASX J1255 and MKT 25413) dwarf satellites. Six galaxies lie on the star-forming main sequence, and their HI gas fractions are typical for such systems. In contrast, MKT 25413 exhibits a log(MHI/Msun) = 5.7, which is the lowest MHI detected of a galaxy that is not a Milky Way satellite. This low surface brightness dwarf galaxy shows an anomalously low level of star formation and low HI fraction for its stellar mass. We also found ubiquitous low column density HI surrounding the galaxies, which is likely a consequence of mild tidal interactions from fly-bys in the past few hundred megayears. We derive the stellar and H$α$ kinematics from VLT/MUSE observations and the H2 kinematics from ALMA observations. The kinematics of the stellar and multiphase interstellar medium of the interacting galaxies display ordered rotation, and the atomic-to-molecular gas ratios are indistinguishable from star-forming field galaxies. The stellar morphology of all the interacting galaxies (apart from the low-mass dwarf UGCA 308) does not show any major disruptions, and there is no stellar component associated with the HI tails, bridges or clouds in the intra-group mediums, down to $μ_{g}$ = 29 mag arcsec$^{-2}$. We surmise that the mild environmental interactions in the close systems have the capacity to pull the diffuse HI out of the disc and redistribute it. The gas is not in equilibrium, although it remains bound and is in the process of falling back onto the disc.

papers.title: Inferring the Total Mass of Galaxy Halos Using Photometry
papers.authors: Chris Brook, Arianna di Cintio, Claudio Dalla Vecchia, Salvador Cardona Barrero, Elena Arjona-Gálvez
papers.abstract: Galaxy size, as defined as the radius at which the stellar surface density reaches $1~\mathrm{M}_\odot\,\mathrm{pc}^{-2}$ ($R_1$), has been shown to correlate more tightly with stellar mass than the effective radius. Cosmological simulations further predict a tight relation between $R_1$ and dark matter halo mass ($M_{200}$), but this prediction has not yet been tested observationally. We present the first observational test of the predicted $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation and assess whether galaxy size, defined through $R_1$, can serve as a robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. We analyze galaxies from the SPARC database, combining high-quality rotation curves to infer dark matter halo masses with stellar surface density profiles derived from photometric data to measure $R_1$. We then compare the observed relation with the predictions from state-of-the-art cosmological simulations. We find good agreement between observations and simulations: galaxies follow the same tight $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation predicted by numerical models across the explored mass range, with low intrinsic scatter. We provide the first observational validation of the $R_1$--$M_{200}$ relation, demonstrating that $R_1$ is a simple, physically motivated, and robust estimator of dark matter halo mass. Because $R_1$ is determined entirely from photometric observations, it provides a tool for inferring halo masses from imaging data alone, with applications to studies of galaxy formation and evolution.

papers.title: A living catalog of stream interaction regions in the Parker Solar Probe era
papers.authors: R. C. Allen, G. C. Ho, L. K. Jian, S. K. Vines, S. D. Bale, A. W. Case, M. E. Hill, C. J. Joyce, J. C. Kasper, K. E. Korreck, D. M. Malaspina, D. J. McComas, R. McNutt, C. Möstl, D. Odstrcil, N. Raouafi, N. A. Schwadron, M. L. Stevens
papers.abstract: Stream interaction regions (SIRs) and corotating interaction regions (CIRs) are important phenomena in heliospheric physics. These large-scale structures vary temporally and spatially, both in latitude and with radial distance. The additions of Parker Solar Probe (PSP) and Solar Orbiter have allowed for investigations into the radial evolution of these structures over a wide range of heliocentric distances for the first time since the Helios era. To better enable investigations of SIRs and CIRs within the inner heliosphere, we have developed a living catalog of SIR and CIR observations by Parker Solar Probe with corresponding observations by STEREO-A as well as ACE and Wind at 1 au. The methodology used for the identification of events and the generation of this catalog, the initial catalog of PSP observations spanning orbits one through five along with corresponding 1 au observations, and information on accessing the living catalog for future studies is described. This list of SIR and CIR events from PSP and corresponding observations from other heliophysics missions will enable case studies utilizing unique orbital arrangements, as well as aid in future statistical studies to further understand the properties and evolution of these structures.

papers.title: Delayed maximum energy solar energetic particle events: Statistical analysis from Solar Orbiter
papers.authors: R. C. Allen, G. C. Ho, G. M. Mason, Z. Ding, M. H. Walker, A. Kouloumvakos, R. F. Wimmer-Schweingruber, J. Rodriguez-Pacheco, S. K. Vines, R. J. Filwett, Z. Xu, C. M. S. Cohen
papers.abstract: Investigations of solar energetic particles (SEPs) have long utilized the dispersive nature of onset times, as in, the earlier arrival of higher-energy particles compared to lower-energy particles, to infer information such as the path length to the acceleration site at the time of initial particle release. However, recent observations by Solar Orbiter and Parker Solar Probe have begun to characterize SEP events with an apparent delay in arrival times of the higher energy portion of the particle distribution, above a critical energy separating the delayed particles from that of the typical velocity dispersion signature at lower energies. Features of these delayed maximum energy (DME) SEP events, sometimes referred to as "inverse velocity dispersion" events, could provide new insight into the impacts of magnetic connectivity to locations along an expanding coronal mass ejection-driven (CME-driven) shock wave, variations of acceleration along the shock surface, and transport effects in the inner heliosphere. This study focuses on the occurrence rate and characteristics of DME events observed by Solar Orbiter relative to their footpoint locations with respect to the initial flare site. These DME events show a bias in occurrence rate towards events when the observer's footpoints were westward of the associated flare location. Additionally, estimated locations at which the highest-energy particles of DME events are released into the flux tube suggest continued release of increasingly higher-energy particles from the CME-driven shock into the connected flux tube well into the inner heliosphere. This indicates that DME events could be attributed to inner heliospheric effects and are not actually coronal in origin. This finding is consistent with previous observations and interpretations of SEP events connected westward of the associated flare.

papers.title: 2:1 Harmonics in the Radio Light Curves of Supermassive Black Hole Binary Candidates
papers.authors: A. C. S. Readhead, M. F. Aller, R. D. Blandford, T. Surti, P. V. De la Parra, A. G. Sullivan, P. Mróz, N. Murray, M. C. Begelman, B. Molina, M. L. Lister, E. R. Most, S. O'Neill, V. A. Diamantopoulos, N. Globus, T. Hovatta, I. Liodakis, T. J. Pearson, S. E. Tremblay
papers.abstract: We present evidence of 2:1 harmonic periodicities in two supermassive black hole binary (SMBHB) candidates (PKS J0805-0111 and PKS 2131-021) in the Owens Valley Radio Observatory (OVRO) + University of Michigan Radio Astronomical Observatory (UMRAO) monitoring programs. This potential discovery follows the previous detection of a 2:1 harmonic periodicity in the SMBHB candidate J1309+1154 from these programs. If confirmed, these suggest a physical origin of blazars exhibiting strong periodicities favoring 2:1 commensurabilities in their light curves. There are significant differences between the 2:1 harmonics in these three blazars, which may be due to differences in their central engines. These three SMBHB candidates demonstrate the importance of careful dissection, i.e. cutting apart and close examination, of blazar light curves, to reveal underlying evidence of coherence between different aspects of the periodicities observed in blazars in the presence of correlated random noise variations. This is particularly important for blazar SMBHB searches, given that the observed periods thus far are all longer than 2 years, and can disappear for long timespans. Harmonics may therefore be crucial in confirming the reality of periodicities and identifying blazar SMBHB candidates. We discuss four models that can account for 2:1 commensurable periodicities in blazar light curves and explain how future detections of shorter period SMBHB candidates, or the lack thereof, may be used to discriminate among the models. Arguments for and against the reality of these periodicities are presented.

papers.title: On the Proper 3D Modeling of Orbits in Wide Binary Gravity Tests
papers.authors: Kyu-Hyun Chae, Hyoseok Park, Youngsub Yoon
papers.abstract: A gravitationally-bound system of wide binary stars with precise 3D relative displacement $\mathbf{r}$ and velocity $\mathbf{v}$ can allow a Keplerian orbit reconstruction for an assumed gravitational parameter $G$. A sufficiently large sample of such systems can also be used to directly infer $G$ specific to the sample. A recent study argued that treating the semi-major axis ($a$) explicitly free with an empirical prior imposed on it can dramatically change the inference of $G$ in the Chae et al. sample of 36 wide binaries. Here we introduce and test a Bayesian Markov chain Monte Carlo algorithm that allows $a$ to be explicitly free (with or without a prior on $a$), and find using the $α$-Cen AB - proxima system and the Chae et al. sample that the explicit-$a$ algorithm with an observational constraint is fully equivalent to the implicit-$a$ algorithm with an internal consistency relation involving the sky-projected separation $s$. For the $α$-Cen AB - proxima system, we present orbits in Milgromian (MOND) as well as Newtonian gravity models. We show that a recent claim of Newtonian gravity from the Chae et al. sample is a consequence of a fatal error in the code or arbitrarily enlarged errors. We discuss how wide binaries can be properly analyzed and modeled to probe gravity at low acceleration and test gravity models, including the necessity of deriving individual-specific parameters, the importance of follow-up observations for anomalous systems, and the relevance of Bayesian MCMC approaches.

papers.title: Developing Environments: Formation and Quenching at Cosmic Noon Traced by the Large-scale Distribution of Gas and Galaxies
papers.authors: Amir H. Khoram, Sirio Belli, Trevor Mendel, Letizia Bugiani, Matteo Sapori, Andrew B. Newman, Hossein Hatamnia, Finn Giddings, Rebecca L. Davies, Olga Cucciati, Bianca Poggianti, Amirnezam Amiri, Minjung Park, Anita Zanella, Tianmu Gao, Gabriel Maheson, Stefano Sotira, Caterina Liboni, Giulia Papini
papers.abstract: Environmental density correlates with galaxy properties in the local Universe, but how and when these trends emerge is unclear: at cosmic noon, large-scale structures are still assembling and galaxies quench rapidly for debated reasons. We study how the formation and quenching histories of massive galaxies at 1.7$<$z$<$3.5 depend on environment, using two independent tracers: galaxy number density ($δ_\#$) from COSMOS-Web and intergalactic neutral hydrogen ($δ_{HI}$, cool gas) from LATIS Ly$α$ tomography. We combine 139 Blue Jay JWST/NIRSpec galaxies with 57 DAWN JWST Archive prism spectra in COSMOS, deriving stellar masses, star formation histories, dust attenuation, and Na\,{\sc d} outflow rates from joint spectro-photometric \texttt{Prospector} fits. In massive quiescent galaxies, the formation-to-quenching interval increases with density. AGN and Na\,{\sc d} outflows are confined to $δ_\#<0.5$ and elevated Ly$α$ absorption ($δ_{HI}>1$), mostly in massive quiescent galaxies showing both. About 65\% of the sample follows a correlation between the tracers; two outlier regions stand out. A galaxy-rich, gas-poor region ($δ_\#>2$, $δ_{HI}<1$) coincides with one of the most massive Hyperion protocluster cores, where the gas is plausibly fully ionized; its quiescent galaxies formed earlier and lack significant AGN activity and outflows. A galaxy-poor, gas-rich region ($δ_\#<1$, $δ_{HI}>1$), within 60 cMpc of the densest Hyperion cores, hosts rapidly quenched galaxies with a high incidence of AGN and outflows. This \emph{developing environment}, distinct from both mature protoclusters and the field, likely traces massive halos still assembling. Galaxy counts alone cannot capture the environment at cosmic noon: jointly mapping galaxies and cool gas is crucial to understand how environment regulates gas accretion, star formation, and quenching.

papers.title: An automated photometric pipeline for measuring the corotation radius of spiral galaxies
papers.authors: Kimia Yazdani, Sahel Mesforoush, Wayne B. Hayes
papers.abstract: The corotation radius R_CR of a spiral galaxy marks the radius where the angular speed of the spiral pattern matches the orbital speed of the disk material. Despite its importance for understanding spiral structure and galaxy evolution, very few galaxies have corotation measurements, often derived using heterogeneous techniques. We present an automated photometric pipeline that identifies corotation radii by tracking the azimuthal phase offset between young and old stellar populations. Building on the color-gradient framework of \citet{Puerari1997}, we extract azimuthal brightness profiles from deprojected dual-band images, fit periodic models to the profiles, and identify corotation candidates at radii where the phase difference between the two stellar tracers changes sign. Each candidate is assigned an adaptive uncertainty interval and reported with a goodness-of-fit metric. We benchmark the method against a cross-method literature compilation, scoring every technique -- including our own -- against a reference built from the published measurements alone and evaluated leave-one-out. Over the $90$ galaxies for which such a reference exists, the pipeline places a correct corotation radius in $80.0\%$ of them, recovers $63.6\%$ of their known corotation radii, and reaches a harmonic mean of recall and purity of $0.58$, the highest values of any method in the comparison. Unlike the published methods, each of which was applied to a small, curated set of galaxies, our pipeline is run on the entire reference sample without any pre-selection, a sample two to six times larger than existing methods. The pipeline is scalable to large surveys, flexible with respect to spiral mode, and naturally recovers multiple corotation radii in galaxies with complex spiral structure, providing a uniform framework for studying disk resonances across diverse galaxy populations.

papers.title: Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems
papers.authors: David Wright, Steve Fetter
papers.abstract: We analyze Fractional Orbital Bombardment Systems (FOBS) as a means of delivering nuclear weapons by placing warheads into partial orbits around the Earth, and show that they do not represent a game-changing advance in technology or capability. We consider potential uses of such a weapon, including evading missile defenses and delivering attacks with short warning time. FOBS could underfly current exoatmospheric defenses, but the required payload reduction may not justify its use if other countermeasures are deemed effective. If a FOBS attack could be successfully disguised as a satellite launch, the warning time could be short enough to raise fears of a decapitating strike. The development of such a capability could lead countries to shorten decision-making timelines in a crisis, which would be destabilizing. The US can take steps to ensure that very-short-warning attacks would not succeed, thereby enhancing deterrence during a crisis.

papers.title: COSMIO: A Benchmark for Cross-Survey Modality Imputation
papers.authors: Dichang Zhang, Yixuan Shao, Jiaqi Deng, Jiali Cui, Haotian Yin, Yuanpeng Liu, Xiang Gao, Zhiqiang Lao, Heather Yu, Simon Birrer, Dimitris Samaras
papers.abstract: Large-scale astronomical surveys define a heterogeneous, partially observed multi-survey learning setting: each object is observed by only a subset of surveys, while survey observations differ in resolutions, wavelength coverage, noise characteristics, and footprints. This setting gives rise to a natural machine learning problem: given observations of an object in some surveys, how to infer its appearance in other surveys. We formalize this as the problem of cross-survey modality imputation and introduce COSMIO, a multi-survey benchmark of aligned observations obtained by forward-rendered shared astrophysical scenes across LSST, Euclid, and Roman under survey-specific instrument characteristics. The benchmark enables systematic evaluation of imputation across source-target survey combinations and missing-survey patterns. We evaluate a broad range of machine learning methods for imputation, which reveal a clear domain gap: methods developed for existing imputation settings transfer poorly to the survey setting. We identify rare-event imputation as a central challenge. This regime arises in the early stages of new surveys, when rare but scientifically valuable phenomena may be available only from prior surveys. We use strong gravitational lensing, where light from a background galaxy is gravitationally deflected by a foreground galaxy, as a representative rare-event setting. We evaluate model performance on zero-shot imputation of gravitational lenses and on downstream scientific tasks using the imputed lens observations. On our constructed evaluation set of galaxy-galaxy strong lenses, performance degrades under rare-event distribution shift, and this degradation further propagates to the downstream lens-detection task. Code: https://github.com/fw-ic/COSMIO.

papers.title: Multimessenger astrophysics drives the case for an Australian Gravitational-Wave observatory
papers.authors: Fiona H. Panther, Paul D. Lasky, Nikhil Sarin
papers.abstract: The next generation of an international network of gravitational-wave observatories is now in the advanced planning stages. With Australia's substantial history of contributions in this field, its history of scientific mega-projects like the Square Kilometer Array, and its unique geographic location and conditions, it is ideally placed to host an observatory in the global network. It has already been demonstrated that a gravitational wave detector in Australia plays an important role in minimizing the sky localization uncertainty of gravitational wave events. We study a particular science case for an Australian observatory, focusing on its potential contributions to multimessenger astronomy. We demonstrate that an observatory in Australia can enable the detection of up to eight multimessenger gravitational-wave plus kilonova events per year, with localisations better than $1-10°^2$ in both second- and third-generation networks. We show that, in a global network of XG observatories, an Australian observatory with 2G sensitivity would still enable significant advances in multimessenger science. The full case for an Australian observatory must be considered in a much broader context; however, this work indicates it could make substantial contributions to multimessenger astrophysics.

papers.title: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the fourth quadrant of the Milky Way
papers.authors: L. -H. Lin, F. Wyrowski, S. Neupane, D. Colombo, K. M. Menten
papers.abstract: The vertical distribution of molecular gas in the Milky Way disk is poorly studied, especially in the 4th quadrant and the far side of the Galaxy. While surveys over 20 years ago suffered from coarse beam and non-Nyquist sampling, most of the recent surveys are limited to $|b|<1^\circ$ and/or focus on the Northern Galactic plane. We examine the molecular gas's vertical distribution and properties in the fourth quadrant to check the impact of Galactic structure on current star formation. We mapped two arm tangent regions ($l=[329^\circ.0,327^\circ.0]$ for the Norma-Outer arm, and $l=[310^\circ.0,308^\circ.5]$ for the Scutum-Centaurus arm) with the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line using the 7-pixel LASMA receiver of the APEX 12 m telescope, covering up to $b=[-2^\circ,+2^\circ]$ (or $|z|\sim200$ pc near the tangent points). The noise level of the $^{12}$CO 3-2 line is about 0.4 K [$T_{MB}$] in velocity channels of 0.5 km s$^{-1}$.
